comparison: Both evaluate claims C3-C8 about PE-specific immune signatures (increased memory-like Th17 cells, memory-like CD8+ T cells, pro-inflammatory macrophages; decreased anti-inflammatory macrophages and gMDSCs). Both find these claims SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes methodological details (CyTOF, sample sizes, statistical methods) and limitations (BMI/gestational age differences, limited GDM&PE samples). Peer reviewers describe findings as 'convincing evidence.' OpenEval also addresses C38 (subset-level changes) which peer reviewers cover separately in R16.

Perfect match on claims C9-C11, C54-C58 regarding correlations between pro-inflammatory macrophages and expanded T cell populations, and negative correlation with gMDSCs. Both find these correlation analyses SUPPORTED. OpenEval appropriately notes that correlation does not establish causation and that the negative correlation with gMDSCs was not statistically significant. Peer Reviewer 1 explicitly acknowledged these correlation findings without concerns.

Both address the overall mechanistic model (C13, C17) involving pro-inflammatory macrophages inducing memory-like Th17 cells via IGF1-IGF1R pathway contributing to PE development and recurrence. OpenEval R19 focuses on IGF1-IGF1R signaling and cell-cell communication (C13, C132-C138), while OpenEval R22 addresses the overall conclusions (C17, C148). Peer R3 encompasses the broader mechanistic findings (C12-C17). Both find SUPPORTED with peer reviewers noting 'convincing evidence' and 'potential translational opportunities.'

Both evaluate IGF1-IGF1R pathway experiments. OpenEval R20 addresses in vitro co-culture experiments (C139-C141) showing IGF1R signaling is necessary for pro-inflammatory macrophage-induced memory-like Th17 differentiation. Peer R4 covers broader IGF1-IGF1R axis findings (C134, C137-C138, C140-C141). Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers emphasize translational potential. OpenEval notes missing details on EV characterization and BMS-754807 concentration.

Perfect match on claims C142-C147 regarding in vivo experiments showing IGF1R signaling in CD4+ T cells is necessary for memory-like Th17 cell induction and PE development. Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers note 'potential translational opportunities' and 'demonstration of adverse effects through in vivo manipulations.' OpenEval notes the use of different PE model (LPS vs RUPP) and missing details on BMS-754807 dosing.

Both address adoptive transfer experiments showing memory-like T cells from PE mice induce PE-like symptoms (C116-C120) and PE recurrence experiments (C122-C127). OpenEval separates these into R16 (development) and R17 (recurrence), while peer R6 covers both aspects together. Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers note findings contribute to 'development and recurrence of PE' and demonstrate 'adverse effects through in vivo manipulations.'

Both address bulk RNA-seq characterization of macrophage phenotypes (C71-C77) and GSEA results (C78-C81). OpenEval R10 covers RNA-seq differential expression, R11 covers GSEA. Peer R7 addresses both together. Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers note 'incorporation of cutting-edge techniques' as strength. OpenEval notes small sample size (n=3) and suggests validation would strengthen findings.

Both evaluate scRNA-seq findings. OpenEval R13 addresses macrophage heterogeneity (C90-C91, C98-C102), while OpenEval R14 addresses memory-like Th17 cell characterization (C12, C103-C107). Peer R8 covers both aspects together (C90-C91, C98-C107). Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers note 'mechanistic insights' and 'identification of specific immune cell populations' as strengths. OpenEval notes missing quality control metrics for scRNA-seq data.

Both address characterization of memory-like Th17 cells including sinusoidal location, checkpoint molecule expression, and activated cytotoxicity (C39-C47). OpenEval covers C39-C49 with flow cytometry, immunofluorescence, and CyTOF validation. Peer R9 covers C39-C42, C44-C45, C47. Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers note this as part of 'identification of specific immune cell populations.' OpenEval notes some interpretations are speculative and would benefit from functional assays.

Both address establishment of PE mouse models. OpenEval R7 covers RUPP model validation (C59-C63), R8 covers adoptive transfer of PE macrophages (C64-C68). Peer R10 covers both aspects (C59-C68) as part of 'utilization of multiple mouse models.' Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes RUPP model appropriately recapitulates PE features; for adoptive transfer, notes missing details on macrophage depletion in recipients.

Perfect match on claims C69-C70 showing macrophages isolated from uterine tissue are predominantly maternal in origin using GFP pregnant mice. Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers note this provides important context for macrophage transfer experiments without raising concerns. OpenEval notes the experimental design (WT female × GFP male) is appropriate for distinguishing maternal from fetal cells.

Perfect match on claims C82-C89 regarding adoptive transfer of pro-inflammatory macrophages inducing PE-like symptoms and immune changes. Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers explicitly note 'demonstration of adverse effects through in vivo manipulations' as strength. OpenEval notes appropriate use of PLX3397 for macrophage depletion with replication using clodronate liposomes, though mentions potential placental barrier crossing as limitation.

Both address characterization of gMDSCs and neutrophils. OpenEval R18 covers scRNA-seq identification of gMDSCs (C15-C16, C128-C131) and notes contradictory GO enrichment results. Peer R13 covers C128-C131 as supporting findings complementing main macrophage/T cell results. Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers note 'identification of specific immune cell populations' as strength without raising concerns about the contradictory enrichment patterns.

Both address cell-cell communication analysis identifying IGF1-IGF1R signaling. OpenEval R19 covers CellPhoneDB analysis and flow cytometry validation (C13, C132-C138). Peer R14 covers computational analysis (C132-C133) supporting macrophage-T cell interactions. Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers note study 'allows for mechanistic insight.' OpenEval notes small human sample size (n=12 NP, n=4 PE) and that computational predictions need experimental validation.

Both address claim C2 that PE is 'usually' complicated by GDM. OpenEval finds claims C1-C2, C18-C22 SUPPORTED but notes C2 'potentially misleading as it overstates the frequency' without specific prevalence data. Peer reviewer finds UNCERTAIN, noting 'usually' may overstate frequency and that GDM is better described as 'common' rather than 'usual' comorbidity. Both identify the same concern about overstating the relationship.

Both address claim C38 that PE-specific changes occur at subset level rather than major population level. OpenEval R3 includes C38 with main PE immune signature findings (C3-C8, C38) and finds SUPPORTED. Peer R16 addresses C38 separately, also finding SUPPORTED and noting 'identification of specific immune cell populations' as strength. Both agree this establishes the specificity of PE-associated immune changes.

OpenEval R11 addresses GSEA results (C78-C81) showing NF-κB enrichment in pro-inflammatory macrophages and tissue development pathways in anti-inflammatory macrophages. Peer R7 addresses broader transcriptional profiling (C71-C81) including both RNA-seq and GSEA. Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers note 'incorporation of cutting-edge techniques' without specific concerns about GSEA interpretations.

OpenEval R14 addresses scRNA-seq characterization of memory-like Th17 cells (C12, C103-C107). Peer R8 covers broader scRNA-seq findings including both macrophages (C90-C91, C98-C102) and T cells (C103-C107). Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers note 'mechanistic insights' and 'identification of specific immune cell populations.' OpenEval provides detailed molecular characterization based on co-expression of Th17 and memory markers.

OpenEval R15 addresses scRNA-seq analysis of memory-like Th17 cells showing differential gene expression and IGF1R upregulation (C108-C114). Peer R8 covers broader scRNA-seq characterization (C90-C107) that includes these findings. Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval specifically notes IGF1R identification as important for subsequent mechanistic studies. Peer reviewers acknowledge mechanistic insights without specific concerns.

OpenEval R17 addresses PE recurrence experiments (C14, C121-C127) showing memory-like Th17 cells contribute to recurrence. Peer R6 covers both development (C116-C120) and recurrence (C122-C127) experiments together. Both find SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers note findings show 'cellular interplay contributed to development and recurrence of PE.' OpenEval notes clinical relevance but indicates mechanism of persistence requires further investigation.

OpenEval R22 presents overall conclusions (C17, C148) synthesizing the complete mechanistic model. Peer R3 addresses the mechanistic findings (C12-C17) including the overall conclusion C17. Both find SUPPORTED with 'convincing evidence.' OpenEval provides comprehensive summary of limitations (BMI/gestational age differences, limited GDM&PE samples, different PE models, PLX3397 effects, lack of functional validation in human samples). Peer reviewers focus on translational potential.

OpenEval R1 addresses background claims about PE and GDM (C1-C2, C18-C22) from introduction, finding them SUPPORTED but noting C2 overstates frequency. Only C2 has corresponding peer evaluation (R15). Other background claims (C1, C18-C22) establishing medical knowledge about PE and GDM have no specific peer review evaluation.

OpenEval R2 addresses extensive background literature review claims (C23-C37) about immune dysregulation in PE and GDM, finding them SUPPORTED as accurate representation of prior work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these literature summary claims.

OpenEval R5 addresses identification of specific macrophage and gMDSC populations by CyTOF (C50-C53), finding SUPPORTED with rigorous multi-parameter phenotyping. No corresponding peer review evaluation found - these specific population identification claims were not separately evaluated by peer reviewers, though related findings appear in other peer evaluations.

OpenEval R8 addresses adoptive transfer of PE-derived macrophages inducing PE-like symptoms (C64-C68), finding SUPPORTED as causal evidence. While peer R10 covers related model establishment claims (C59-C68), the specific adoptive transfer experiment (C64-C68) is not separately distinguished in peer reviews from RUPP model validation (C59-C63).
